paper.title: Optimal Best-Arm Identification in Bandits with Access to Offline Data

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed-confidence best-arm identification with offline data (offline-online paradigm), SPEF arms
unmapped: learner has access to tau_1 offline samples from the same instance, collected by an unknown adaptive offline policy; tau_1 may depend on delta
delta-correctness is with respect to the joint distribution of offline and online data; sample complexity counts online samples only
conditional delta-correctness (given each offline history) variant discussed in Appendix B (Theorem B.2, Bernoulli arms): online lower bound unchanged, not recorded as a scalar result
settings.definition_quote: In addition to the unknown bandit instance $\mu$ from which the algorithm can generate samples, it has access to $\tau_1$ samples from the arms in $\mu$. We refer to these historical samples as the offline data ... we are interested in an online policy that stops at time $\tau_1 + \tau_\delta>0$ and outputs a best arm estimate $k_{\tau_1 + \tau_\delta}$ such that $\mathbb{P}(k_{\tau_1 + \tau_\delta} \neq 1 ) \leq \delta $

settings.name_in_paper: Offline-online regret minimization (lower bound), SPEF arms
unmapped: learner has access to offline samples N^o_a(T) collected by an independent adaptive policy; regret counts online pulls only
settings.definition_quote: In addition, it also has access to samples generated from the same set of $K$ distributions using some adaptive policy that is independent of the algorithm. We refer to these additional samples as `offline data'

settings.name_in_paper: Offline-online regret minimization with unit-variance Gaussian arms (o-o UCB)
unmapped: learner has N^o_a offline samples per arm, used in the UCB index
settings.definition_quote: For simplicity, in this section, we assume that the arms have Gaussian distributions with unit variance ... The algorithm has access to $N^o_a$ offline samples from each arm.

symbols.T_P1: optimal value of problem P1: min sum_a N_a s.t. inf_x {(E[N^o_1]+N_1)KL(mu_1,x)+(E[N^o_a]+N_a)KL(mu_a,x)} >= log(1/(2.4 delta)) for all a != 1

conditions: arm 1 is the unique best arm

source.label: thm:Lower_bound
source.quote: For all $\mu \in {\cal S}^K$, $\mu_1 > \mu_{a}$, $a \ne 1$, a $\delta$-correct policy satisfies: $\mathbb{E}[\tau_\delta] \geq T^{*}$.

results.notes: Bound on expected number of online samples; T* depends on expected offline counts. Equivalent to tau_1/z* - tau_1 in normalized form.

conditions: arm 1 is the unique best arm
tuning: GLRT stopping threshold beta(t,delta) = log((K-1)/delta) + 6 log(log(t/2)+1) + 8 log(1+log((K-1)/delta))

source.label: thm:delta-correct
source.quote: Over the randomness in offline samples, (unknown) offline policy, online policy, and samples, the algorithm proposed is $\delta$-correct.

results.notes: delta-correctness statement, recorded as error probability <= delta.

bound.regime: up to an additive o(log(1/delta)) term

symbols.z_star: optimal offline fraction from problem P3 (lower bound on E[tau_delta]+tau_1 equals tau_1/z_star)
symbols.alpha_eps: alpha(eps'), continuous with alpha(eps')->0 as eps'->0
symbols.C_mu: C(mu, p_hat, eta), instance-dependent constant, positive for eta>0

conditions: tau_1/(log(1/delta)+log log(1/delta)) not in (C_1^a(c_eps1), C_2^a(c_eps',eps~)) for all a != 1
arm 1 is the unique best arm

source.label: thm:stop_bound1
source.quote: For $\delta > 0$, suppose $\mu\in\mathcal S^K$ is such that $ 1 \ge z^*(\mu) > \eta$, for some $\eta > 0$. ... then the algorithm satisfies: \[ \mathbb{E}[\tau_{\delta}] + \tau_1 \le \frac{\tau_1}{z^*}\lrp{1 + \frac{2\alpha(\epsilon') + \tilde{\epsilon}}{\epsilon_1 C(\mu,\hat{p},\eta)} } + T(\epsilon') + T(\tilde{\epsilon}) + 1 + o\lrp{\log\frac{1}{\delta}}.\]

results.notes: Bound on online + offline samples; the o(log 1/delta) term is omitted from the expression. Appendix restatement (Theorem E.1) puts an expectation over offline proportions p_hat on the main term. The discussion shows that as delta->0, letting eps',eps~->0, limsup (E[tau_delta]+tau_1)/log(1/delta) <= limsup tau_1/(z* log(1/delta)), matching the lower bound (asymptotic optimality).

conditions: consistent algorithm: E[N_a(T)] = o(T^alpha) for all alpha>0, all suboptimal a, all instances
bound applies to offline plus online pulls of each suboptimal arm a

source.quote: For $\mu\in\mathcal S^K$ with $a^*(\mu) = 1$, any consistent algorithm satisfies \[ \liminf\limits_{T\rightarrow \infty} \frac{\E\lrs{N^o_a(T)} + \E\lrs{N_a(T)}}{\log T} \ge \frac{1}{\KL(\mu_a, \mu_1)}. \]

results.notes: Pull-count lower bound (per suboptimal arm) including offline samples; quantity 'other'.

bound.regime: up to an additive o(log T) term; outer expectation over offline count N^o_a

symbols.N_o_i: number of offline samples of arm i (random; expectation taken over it)

conditions: bound on online pulls of suboptimal arm a
tuning: index U_a(t) = mu_hat_a(t) + sqrt(4 log t/(N^o_a + N_a(t)))

source.quote: For $\mu\in\mathcal S^K$ with $a^*(\mu) = 1$, \texttt{o-o UCB} has the following bound on the number of pulls of sub-optimal arm $a$ till time $T$: \[ \E\lrs{N_a(T) } \le \E\lrs{\max\lrset{1, \frac{8\log T}{\Delta^2_a} - {N}^o_a + 1}} + o(\log T). \]

results.notes: Pull-count bound; regret = sum_a Delta_a E[N_a(T)]. o(log T) omitted from expression. Proof sketched via Auer et al. 2002.
